supporting_observations.claim: The large transfer in the records is a 640,000,000-byte outbound proxy tunnel to ingest.safeharbor-backup.net, with only 39,000 bytes returning; the transfer began at 13:50:30 UTC, not around the alert's stated 13:46 UTC.
Immediately before the transfer, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket event for svc-vault from public IP 139.162.174.124; FILE-MAP-01 then logged a svc-vault service logon.
The Safeharbor agent ran as svc-vault under the same logon ID as that service logon and initiated the large upload about a minute later.

Although Safeharbor and its agent are approved and the transfer destination matches the approved backup service, the preceding svc-vault authentication from a public IP is inconsistent with the stated environment (no VPN; remote administration only from WS-AHASSAN-01). The close account, process, and transfer linkage makes this transfer suspicious despite the approved tool and destination.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records show proxy tunnel byte counts and a related GET, but not the contents of the uploaded data.
The supplied records do not establish whether the svc-vault ticket request from the public IP was authorized or how it occurred.
The bulk upload recorded here starts at 13:50:30 UTC, several minutes after the alert's stated approximate time; the records do not explain that timing difference.
The records identify the agent path and command line but provide no file hash, signature-validation result, or backup-job configuration to independently verify the executable and job.
claims_not_established: That the uploaded data was stolen, sensitive, or outside the intended backup set.
That the public IP event was definitively an attacker rather than a logging, routing, or other anomaly.
That the alert's stated 13:46 time corresponds to the 13:50:30 transfer in the records.
additional_evidence_needed: Correlate the alert's original flow/time with proxy and network telemetry to resolve the 13:46 versus 13:50:30 discrepancy.
Review domain-controller authentication details and perimeter/network records for the svc-vault ticket request from 139.162.174.124; validate whether that source is legitimate.
Collect Safeharbor job schedules, backup manifests, service configuration, and agent hash/signature validation to determine whether this upload was expected and what data it contained.
Review svc-vault credential use and changes around the event, including relevant account, service, and endpoint audit records.
unrelated_findings: greta.lund initiated an RDP session to FILE-MAP-01 from WS-GLUND-01, although the stated remote-administration practice assigns that activity to ali.hassan from WS-AHASSAN-01. This is a separate access review and is not used to decide the transfer alert. (T150-00286, T150-00293, T150-00298)

FILE-MAP-01 made proxy connections labeled GlobalProtect and Zscaler Client Connector, neither of which is listed as approved in the supplied inventory. Investigate separately; these connections do not establish the cause of the Safeharbor transfer. (T150-00308, T150-00596)
